title: Collections Desk Decision Table: Catch-Up Days by Delinquency and Tenure
content:
A cure payment on Kestrel Auto Finance Retail Installment Contracts also carries a catch-up amount, applied to principal, equal to one day's interest on the principal balance at the contract APR over the tier's day-count basis multiplied by the catch-up days and rounded to the cent.

The catch-up days start from the delinquency and the tenure of the contract. Days past due are the calendar days from the next due date on the contract record to the payment date; the installments paid are the contract's scheduled-installment payments less its returned payments, as the loan history shows them.

## Decision table

| Days past due | Installments paid | Starting catch-up days |
|---|---|---|
| 30 or more | fewer than 24 | short-tenure catch-up days: 10 |
| 30 or more | 24 or more | long-tenure catch-up days: 5 |
| fewer than 30 | any | none |

## Boundary cases (hypothetical)

- 29 days past due, 8 installments paid: none.
- 30 days past due, 23 installments paid: 10 days.
- 30 days past due, 24 installments paid: 5 days.
- 26 scheduled-installment payments and 3 returned payments: 23 installments paid, so the short-tenure row applies.

## Worked figure (hypothetical)

Principal balance 14200.00 at 19.59 percent over a 365-day basis gives one day's interest of 7.6213; 10 catch-up days give a catch-up amount of 76.21, and 5 days give 38.11.
